title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
description: Call, text, or chat for support with emotional distress or a crisis.
howTo: Call or text 988, or use the website to chat with a counselor.
importantNotes: For immediate danger or a medical emergency, call 911.

title: Crisis Text Line
description: Free crisis support by text.
howTo: Text HOME to 741741 to connect with a crisis counselor.

title: The Trevor Project
description: Crisis support for LGBTQ+ young people.
howTo: Call, text START to 678678, or use the website for online chat.

title: Trans Lifeline
description: Peer phone support for transgender and questioning people.
howTo: Check the hotline's current hours, then call to speak with a peer supporter.
importantNotes: This service is not available 24/7; check current hours on its website.

title: Paper SNAP and benefits application (BFA 800)
description: Paper NH DHHS application for SNAP and other assistance.
howTo: Print the form, complete the sections that apply, and follow its instructions to submit it to NH DHHS.
importantNotes: The form covers several programs. NH DHHS may require an interview and supporting documents.

title: NH Food Bank food finder
description: Find food assistance and mobile pantries.
howTo: Search local food resources or check the mobile pantry schedule.

title: 211 New Hampshire
description: Find food, housing, utility, legal and other local help.
howTo: Search by need and location, or call to speak with a resource specialist.

title: United Way — Tech Access for All
description: Technology help and access to devices in Greater Nashua.
howTo: Review current device-access and technology-support options, then follow the program's contact instructions.
importantNotes: Population: Not confirmed. Approximate city/town pin only; not the property location. Contact the provider for the address before traveling.

title: Nashua Soup Kitchen & Shelter — Shelter Access
description: Emergency shelter access for single adults and families with children.
howTo: Call 603-889-7770, extension 1138, on weekdays. After hours or weekends, call 211.
importantNotes: Public contact point shown; call outreach for shelter placement and the correct arrival location. A map pin does not mean a bed is available.

title: Families in Transition — Adult Emergency Shelter
description: Emergency shelter and housing support for adults experiencing homelessness.
howTo: Call 211 first for coordinated shelter access and placement instructions.
importantNotes: Call before traveling; beds and admission requirements vary.

title: Cross Roads House
description: Emergency and transitional shelter with support for adults and families.
howTo: Call 211 first for shelter referrals. Shelter staff can answer questions at 603-436-2218, 24/7.
importantNotes: Placement depends on availability and assessment; call before traveling.

title: Hundred Nights — Emergency Shelter
description: Year-round emergency shelter and a daytime resource center for individuals and families.
howTo: Call and ask for the Intake Office to discuss available beds and entry requirements.
importantNotes: Year-round service; call before traveling. Resource-center visitor hours differ from overnight shelter access.

title: My Friend's Place
description: Emergency shelter and transitional housing support for individuals and families.
howTo: Call to discuss your situation, eligibility, and current shelter availability.
importantNotes: Call before traveling; a listing does not guarantee placement.

title: Belknap House — Family Shelter
description: Year-round shelter and case management for families with children in Belknap County.
howTo: Call about eligibility and ask your local welfare office for the required referral.
importantNotes: Family shelter. A welfare-office referral is required; contact staff about room availability.

title: Concord Coalition — Shelter & Housing Access
description: Daytime homeless resource center offering housing support and information about seasonal winter shelter.
howTo: Call for resource-center access and current winter-shelter arrangements. For urgent shelter referrals, call 211.
importantNotes: This pin marks the resource center. Winter shelter is seasonal, generally December–March; confirm dates and entry instructions.

title: Nashua Soup Kitchen & Shelter — Food Pantry
description: Groceries, fresh produce, and food boxes for people needing food assistance.
howTo: Bring your own shopping bags. Call if you cannot attend the listed hours.
importantNotes: Hours: Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri 11 AM–2:45 PM; Tue 6–7 PM; third Sun 2:30–4 PM. Produce: up to twice weekly; food box: monthly.

title: Corpus Christi Food Pantry
description: Food pantry serving the Nashua community.
howTo: Call for an appointment before visiting.
importantNotes: Hours by appointment: Mon/Wed 10 AM–noon; Tue/Thu 2–4 PM. Closed on listed holidays.

title: Families in Transition — Food Pantry
description: Choice-based grocery pantry for Manchester individuals and families.
howTo: First visit: bring photo ID and proof of Manchester residence. Returning visitors: bring your pantry card.
importantNotes: Hours: Mon 1–4 PM; Tue–Fri 10 AM–noon and 1–4 PM. Closed weekends. Grocery visits every 30 days.

title: Gather — Pantry Market
description: Free groceries and prepared take-home meals for people living or working in New Hampshire or Maine.
howTo: Bring proof of NH or Maine residence or employment. You can register and shop on your first visit.
importantNotes: Hours: Mon–Thu 10 AM–4 PM; Fri 10 AM–2 PM.

title: SHARE Outreach — Food Pantry
description: Food and other assistance for residents of Milford, Amherst, Brookline, and Mont Vernon.
howTo: Call the main office to schedule a food-pantry appointment.
importantNotes: Pantry by appointment. Office hours: Mon–Fri 8:30 AM–4:30 PM; call ahead.

title: St. Vincent de Paul — Exeter Pantry
description: Emergency groceries and community assistance in the Exeter area.
howTo: Call about registration and your household's needs. Tuesday visits require an appointment.
importantNotes: Hours: Mon/Wed/Fri 10 AM–noon; Mon/Wed 7–8 PM; Tue by appointment. Weather and holiday closures apply.

title: The Community Kitchen — Keene Pantry & Meals
description: Weekly grocery distributions and weekday hot meals.
howTo: Use the drive-through on Wednesday or walk-through on Thursday. Call about registration or special food needs.
importantNotes: Pantry: Wed 12:30–5:30 PM drive-through; Thu 11:30 AM–4 PM walk-through. Hot meals: Mon–Fri 5–6:20 PM.

title: CAPSC — Dover Food Pantry
description: Short-term grocery assistance through Community Action Partnership of Strafford County.
howTo: Visit during pantry hours or call extension 8136. Tell staff about dietary needs or lack of refrigeration.
importantNotes: Hours: Mon–Fri 8:30 AM–4:30 PM.

title: CAPSC — Rochester Food Pantry
description: Grocery assistance with a self-shopping option in Rochester.
howTo: Visit during pantry hours or call extension 8136 about food needs.
importantNotes: Hours: Tuesday noon–2 PM.

title: St. Vincent de Paul — Laconia Pantry
description: Monthly food assistance for households in the Lakes Region.
howTo: Call the pantry before visiting to confirm its schedule and registration requirements.
importantNotes: Confirmed published hours: Monday noon–2 PM. Call about any additional evening sessions.

title: The Friendly Kitchen — Concord Meals
description: Free prepared meals in a welcoming setting; everyone is welcome.
howTo: Come during meal service. This is a meal site rather than a grocery pantry.
importantNotes: Meals: lunch Mon–Fri noon–12:45 PM; dinner daily 5–5:45 PM; breakfast Sat/Sun 8–8:45 AM. Check the website for seasonal breakfast changes.

title: NH Food Bank — Mobile Pantry Schedule
description: Find upcoming drive-through food distributions across New Hampshire.
howTo: Check the current date, location, and time before traveling.
importantNotes: First come, first served while supplies last. No ID required. Locations and dates change.
